questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Please explain: *
questions.answer: The Blended Intensive Programme (BIP) gave academic opportunities, but what motivated me the most was that most of the classes took place physically in the city we were reading about and studying as a historical place. Also, there was an important social aspect of the study trip abroad and I enjoyed being away from home for a short intensive period of time.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination and the topic of the Blended Intensive Programme (BIP) were planned together by the instructors and formed a whole.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As the BIP were a co-operation between my home university, another visiting university and the host university in Germany, the registration process were done mostly by my home university (as far as I remember).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My fellow students in Copenhagen and I helped each other in many of the practical arrangements, for instance laying out the travel plan. Our instructor from Copenhagen were available and helpful, as well as the Associate Professor from the host institution.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think all international students experienced more group work than we were used to. And we enjoyed it. Because it was in connection with and followed up by more traditional lectures with power point slides as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not experience the every day life on Halle-Wittenberg University campus, but the conference center and facilities in Wittenberg were good and the people were very accommodating.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The students from Halle-Wittenberg were very accessible in conversation, diligent and helpful hosts.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I read and learned a lot during the week in Wittenberg and at the same time I had fun with my fellow students in the small town. The concentrated stay abroad was very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It is of great advantage to have read the syllabus before you attend the physical lessons during the BIP. I had to read some of the texts from day to day, and that was challenging as the week is quite eventful.
